gaps: No fish or seafood in the collection at all — a major protein gap.
No Korean cuisine despite having the wok and the palate for bold fermented flavors.
No Japanese cuisine, and the carbon-steel wok and gas range are ideal for it.
North Indian cuisine is absent; the collection has South Indian (kanji) but nothing from the Punjabi canon.
The Big Green Egg appears in the equipment list but is not used in any current recipe — no low-and-slow smoke project.
Egg-based mains are missing entirely — a fast, vegetarian-friendly gap on weeknights.
Chinese fried rice, the highest-wok-skill weeknight workhorse, is not in the collection.

ideas.title: Miso Salmon in Foil
ideas.why: Fills the complete absence of fish in the collection with a fast, sheet-pan-friendly Japanese technique that cooks in 30 minutes.

ideas.title: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice with Vegetables)
ideas.why: Opens the Korean cuisine gap entirely absent from the collection; the beef is a small garnish easily omitted for the vegetarian adult.

ideas.title: Okonomiyaki (Savory Japanese Cabbage Pancake)
ideas.why: Adds a Japanese egg-and-vegetable main cooked on the cast iron that works as-written without any protein, or with bacon on top for the non-vegetarian adults — aligning perfectly with the household's 'we eat bacon' note.

ideas.title: Dal Makhani (Restaurant-Style Black Lentil Dal)
ideas.why: Fills the North Indian gap that the South Indian kanji doesn't cover — a slow-simmered Punjabi lentil dish that is fully vegetarian and makes a big batch for six.

ideas.title: Shakshuka
ideas.why: Adds an egg-based weeknight main that is fully vegetarian as written — a technique and protein form (eggs poached in sauce) completely absent from the current collection.

ideas.title: Texas-Style Smoked Beef Brisket
ideas.why: The Big Green Egg is sitting unused in the collection's equipment list — this is the canonical low-and-slow project that finally puts it to work, adding a weekend smoke tradition for the household.
